findings.reason: the deliverable has two parts and the gate measures only one, so the node can be closed while half its deliverable is undone; adding a clause the unification must satisfy (the predicate defined once and referenced by both builders) closes it.
findings.text: §21's done-when requires only that the file "holds a case for the inline-rename branch, and every test in the file passes, the inventory test included with its expected set unchanged"; it names no check that the exclusive-create predicate was actually collapsed from its two copies at `reckon/interface_counts.py:319` and `:382` to one, so a worker may add the test, leave the duplication untouched, and still pass every clause — closing the first of §20's two follow-ons unaddressed

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — the cited module `reckon/interface_counts.py` and test `tests/test_staged_write_inventory.py` both exist, and the new document-level evidence href resolves to `#s20-claim-move-aside-not-staged` in the landed archive.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §21's done-when measures only its second deliverable (the new inline-rename case and its control) and carries no clause that the duplicated exclusive-create predicate was collapsed to one.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — the negative control is logged under the run directory, a durable path a later reader can open, as every other section in this plan does.
rubric_items.naming: pass — §21 introduces no plan label, stage name, ticket number or version tag; its prose names mechanisms (`exclusive_creators`, `not_created`, `local - callers_not_staging[name]`).
rubric_items.reasoning: pass — the stated root cause (a predicate spelled twice, and an untested inline branch) matches the §20 review it cites and the code at `interface_counts.py:319`, `:362` and `:382`; the mechanism (a single predicate plus a new test case) can produce the done-when, and the test runs on the real path (`_staged_writes` over `tests/test_staged_write_inventory.py`).
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §21's two items (collapse the duplicated predicate, add the inline-branch case) serve one goal, the delegated move-aside exemption expressed once and covered on both branches, and both are closeable on one verdict once the done-when clause is added.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — §21 is declared `implementable` and the sole open followup `f-ashenr-021` (`plan.html:267`) recommends `/reckon-build a-seat-held-elsewhere-is-not-restarted §21`; §20 it depends on is `done`, so no gate is owed.
